# Wealth Insights Generator Agent — Production Runbook

> **Scenario**: Wealth Insights Generator Agent
> **Platform**: Microsoft Copilot Studio — GitHub Copilot harness
> **Target readers**: Makers, delivery engineers, customer or partner operators

**Estimated effort**: Not yet measured; record actual effort on the Frontier Clock.

**Template:** an example to modify for your requirements; the customer or partner wires it into their environment. See the [Overview](1.Overview.md).

## Prerequisites

| Requirement | Details | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Build workload | 20 captured build checkpoints; 5 skills; 2 knowledge files; 7 acceptance checks; 5 locked cases. [Inventory](2.Architecture.md#copilot-studio-components), [checks](0.Resources/README.md#template-acceptance-checks), and [cases](4.Sample-prompts.md#demo-prompts). | Template |
| Licensing and capacity | Confirm tenant licensing and Copilot Credits for the GitHub Copilot harness; building, Preview and evaluation consume credits before publication. | Customer or partner |
| Environment and maker access | Record the approved environment, publisher prefix and maker access; confirm the reviewed Sonnet46 model and keep the workshop synthetic and Draft. | Customer or partner |
| DLP and data policy | Have the administrator review uploaded files, proposed CRM, aggregation, planning, Outlook and Teams connectors, and channels; document blocked paths. | Customer or partner |
| Identity and audience | Review the supplied GroupMembership access policy, Integrated authentication and Always trigger; record who builds, tests and later uses the agent. | Customer or partner |
| Connection ownership | Name owners for CRM, aggregation, planning and collaboration connections with dedicated references; the synthetic workshop needs none. | Customer or partner |
| Test identities | Prepare advisor, relationship-manager, director, strategist and denied-access identities for an approved test deployment; makers use Draft Preview. | Customer or partner |
| Tooling by build lane | Manual lane: Copilot Studio in the browser and the reviewed files. Easy mode: GitHub Copilot in VS Code Agent mode, the Copilot Studio plugin and a supported PAC CLI. | Customer or partner |
| Advice and disclosure ownership | Have compliance approve the advice, suitability, freshness, consent and specialist gates before client data replaces the synthetic records. | Customer or partner |

## Phase 0 — Qualify and Adapt the Template

### Step 0-1. Qualify the outcome and baseline

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Wealth business owner

Complete the [qualification checklist](1.Overview.md#qualification-checklist).

**Measure:** Advisor preparation: how relationship, held-away asset, planning and life-event context is gathered before client reviews. Agree where research time and incomplete data lead to generic or premature guidance before attributing change to the agent.

Fill your baseline record:

| Household | Systems consulted | Held-away data available | Life events on record | Planning signals reviewed | Specialist referrals | Advisor |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

Agree replacement connections, governance, telemetry, support and success measures before production.

### Step 0-2. Adapt scope and name owners

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Wealth business owner

Adapt [scope](1.Overview.md#in-scope--out-of-scope) and the [data contract](2.Architecture.md#data-contract); assign approval roles.

| Role | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| Wealth business owner | Approve advisor-facing scope, data replacements, review gates and success measures; keep synthetic figures out of customer results. |
| Licensed advisors and specialist reviewers | Validate facts, suitability, consent and disclosures, with compliance, tax, legal, estate or trading review as applicable. |
| Copilot Studio maker | Build the reviewed instructions, two knowledge files and five skills; remove web search, confirm the model and keep the agent Draft. |
| Power Platform administrator | Confirm licensing, capacity, maker access, authenticated audience and data policies before any wealth connection is approved. |
| Wealth data and connection owners | Approve CRM, aggregation, planning, Outlook and Teams access; record dedicated least-privilege connection references. |
| Acceptance reviewer | Check WIG-01 through WIG-05, the boundary tests and Easy/Manual parity; reject markers visible only in reasoning text. |
| Operations owner | Own production support, session and credit monitoring and configuration recovery; route client decisions to licensed advisors. |

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Replacement connections, governance, telemetry, support and success measures for advisor preparation are agreed.
- [ ] The business owner records how advisors assemble client, asset and planning context today before choosing success measures.

## Phase 1 — Environment, Identity and Access

### Step 1-1. Approve the identity and settings design

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Review and approve the [identity design](2.Architecture.md#identity-and-permissions) and [template settings](../../solutions/wealth-insights-generator/copilot-studio/settings.mcs.yml). Apply agent-specific settings when the agent is built in [Phase 2](#phase-2--build-and-prove-the-agent).

Approve document, connector and channel policies; require authentication and verify blocked routes stay blocked.

### Step 1-2. Configure tenant controls

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Approve the environment, audience and connection identities. Define the [authentication plan](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/configuration-end-user-authentication); configure environment [data policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/admin-data-loss-prevention).

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The target environment and approved publisher prefix are recorded, with maker access granted, before any build starts.
- [ ] The authenticated advisor audience and least-privilege scopes for client, asset and planning data are approved.

## Phase 2 — Build and Prove the Agent

### Step 2-1. Choose the build lane

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

| Lane | Suits | Output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Easy mode with GitHub Copilot (default) | Assisted authoring | Synthetic Draft proof |
| Manual build in Copilot Studio | Browser-only makers | Same Draft proof |
| AIBAST Frontier (experimental) | Portable learning | Behavior proof; native validation follows |

[Compare lanes](1.Overview.md#delivery-lanes); local Brainstem remains optional.

### Step 2-2. Build the selected implementation

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

**Easy mode:** use the [authoring skill](../../skills/aibast-easy-mode-copilot/SKILL.md) and [reviewed messages](../../solutions/wealth-insights-generator/EASY-MODE-COPILOT-CHAT.md). **Manual:** use the [single inventory](2.Architecture.md#copilot-studio-components) and [tutorial](https://microsoft.github.io/aibast-agents-library/solutions/wealth-insights-generator/manual-tutorial.html) with the checklist below. **Portable learning:** follow [deployment.json](../../solutions/wealth-insights-generator/deployment.json); it does not replace native Draft validation.

**Manual build checklist** — [captured sequence](../../solutions/wealth-insights-generator/screenshots/manual/browserfilm.json). Record current results.

1. Create a blank Copilot Studio agent
2. Name Wealth Insights Manual
3. Enter the reviewed global instructions
4. Save the instruction policy
5. Remove default web search
6. Add knowledge: aibast_wealth-insights-generator-controls-and-review.md
7. Add knowledge: aibast_wealth-insights-generator-synthetic-records.md
8. Add skill: aibast_client-insights_02
9. Add skill: aibast_market-brief_01
10. Add skill: aibast_meeting-brief_05
11. Add skill: aibast_opportunity-alerts_03
12. Add skill: aibast_performance-attribution_04
13. Review model, skills, knowledge, and safety boundaries
14. Open a fresh Preview conversation
15. Pass WIG-01: Advisory Director
16. Pass WIG-02: Wealth Advisor
17. Pass WIG-03: Relationship Manager
18. Pass WIG-04: Portfolio Strategist
19. Pass WIG-05: Wealth Advisor
20. Confirm Draft and stop before publish

### Step 2-3. Enforce workshop integrity

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Apply the [workshop integrity and recovery rules](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery) before replay.

### Step 2-4. Replay the synthetic proof

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

**Synthetic demo acceptance:** record every locked case: WIG-01, WIG-02, WIG-03, WIG-04, WIG-05. Use the [acceptance matrix](4.Sample-prompts.md#per-case-acceptance-matrix) and [template acceptance checks](0.Resources/README.md#template-acceptance-checks).

### Exit criteria

- [ ] This lane's Preview evidence identifies the agent, environment, model, inventory, cases and Draft state.
- [ ] If the portable lane is chosen, its smoke test calls `WealthInsightsGeneratorAgent` and returns the required markers.
- [ ] If built manually, the Draft has the reviewed instructions, two knowledge files, five skills and the confirmed model; web search and tools are absent.
- [ ] Unchanged WIG-01 through WIG-05 prompts pass, each in a separate fresh Preview conversation on the owned Draft.
- [ ] Each case passes on its final answer; markers seen only in reasoning text are not proof.

## Phase 3 — Wire In Your Systems

<a id="shared-integration-controls"></a>

**Shared identity and scope controls**

For each integration, decide end-user versus approved maker/service credentials. [Configure authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/configuration-end-user-authentication) for the [authorized audience](2.Architecture.md#identity-and-permissions).

**Shared scope:** Require sign-in before exposing client, asset or planning data. Request only the read scopes the approved wealth sources need. Restrict the audience and test authorized and denied identities. Enforce these restrictions at each connection.

### Step 3-1. Integrate Dynamics 365 wealth-management CRM

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Wealth data and connection owners

1. **Bind Dynamics 365 wealth-management CRM — read:** Bind approved read-only connector actions for relationship records.

2. **Identity for Dynamics 365 wealth-management CRM:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Dynamics 365 wealth-management CRM:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Dynamics 365 wealth-management CRM:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 2](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Send and schedule nothing; the brief is preparation material for advisor review. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Reject it; never substitute a household or fabricate evidence.

### Step 3-2. Integrate Approved portfolio aggregation and held-away asset data

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Wealth data and connection owners

1. **Bind Approved portfolio aggregation and held-away asset data — read:** Expose read-only aggregation lookups through a custom connector.

2. **Identity for Approved portfolio aggregation and held-away asset data:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Approved portfolio aggregation and held-away asset data:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Approved portfolio aggregation and held-away asset data:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 5](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Create nothing and update no CRM record; present the insight for advisor review. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Reject it; never substitute a household or fabricate evidence.

### Step 3-3. Integrate Financial planning and performance systems

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Wealth data and connection owners

1. **Bind Financial planning and performance systems — read:** Bind approved read-only connector or API actions.

2. **Identity for Financial planning and performance systems:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Financial planning and performance systems:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Financial planning and performance systems:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 4](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Place no order or transaction; show attribution context for review. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Report unavailable evidence; never claim a lookup, outreach, CRM change or order succeeded.

### Step 3-4. Integrate Microsoft Outlook

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Wealth data and connection owners

1. **Bind Microsoft Outlook — write:** Keep sending and scheduling unavailable; gate any draft workflow behind licensed-advisor review (preview).

2. **Identity for Microsoft Outlook:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Microsoft Outlook:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Microsoft Outlook:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 2](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Send and schedule nothing; the brief is preparation material for advisor review. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Return preparation material and name the licensed reviewer; perform no action.

### Step 3-5. Integrate Microsoft Teams specialist review

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Wealth data and connection owners

1. **Bind Microsoft Teams specialist review — write:** Gate any review-request workflow behind human approval (preview).

2. **Identity for Microsoft Teams specialist review:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Microsoft Teams specialist review:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Microsoft Teams specialist review:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 8](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Retry the named skill once in the same turn; if it still fails, say so and stop without an uncited answer. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Return preparation material and name the licensed reviewer; perform no action.

### Step 3-6. Connect

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Wealth data and connection owners

Bind approved least-privilege connection references only; keep consequential actions behind explicit approval.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Approved CRM, aggregation, planning, Outlook and Teams connections replace the synthetic inputs and preserve the reviewed input and output contract.
- [ ] Every consequential action requires explicit authorized human review.

## Phase 4 — Evaluate on Your Data

### Step 4-1. Adapt the evaluation corpus

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Preserve [locked behaviors](4.Sample-prompts.md#per-case-acceptance-matrix) and [boundary tests](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases) when substituting approved customer fixtures.

### Step 4-2. Set thresholds and evaluate your data

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Have the business owner approve thresholds. Run [adapted evaluations (preview)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/analytics-agent-evaluation-intro) before publication under approved test user profiles. Keep exact assertions separate from General quality scores.

Test an approved deployment as advisor personas and an unshared identity; maker access does not prove user access.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The business owner sets customer-data acceptance measures; synthetic returns, alpha and assets are not production thresholds.
- [ ] Adapted evaluations record the tested version and user profile; General quality scoring does not replace exact assertions.

## Phase 5 — Pilot and Rollout

### Step 5-1. Review the template release prerequisites

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

These synthetic regression gates do not set production thresholds. The reference workshop stays Draft; production approval belongs to the customer pilot.

| Template gate | Required evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Locked wealth corpus | All five cases, WIG-01 through WIG-05, satisfy every required and forbidden marker. |
| Manual inventory | Two knowledge files, five skills and the reviewed model; no tools or web search. |
| Regulated boundary | Any advice, suitability finding, current-market claim, outreach, CRM change, order or transaction is no-go. |
| Visual evidence | Require final-answer anchors; reasoning-only and reshoot-required frames cannot pass. |
| Release state | The manual and pilot agents are Draft with `published: false`. |

### Step 5-2. Publish and share deliberately

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Wealth business owner

With business approval, [publish and share](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/authoring-share-agent) the adapted build with a restricted test audience. Keep the reference workshop Draft.

Require explicit confirmation before the production publish operation.

### Step 5-3. Run the governed pilot

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Wealth business owner

**Pilot entry gate:** Test allowed and denied identities on the published, shared agent; resolve access failures before admitting pilot users. Compare pilot results with the baseline and thresholds; broaden rollout only after go/no-go.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Synthetic labels, human review and no-advice, no-approval and no-transaction behavior are validated, and publication is explicitly confirmed.
- [ ] The approved advisor audience and supported channels are tested before publication is confirmed.

## Phase 6 — Operate

### Step 6-1. Retain the operational playbook

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Operations owner

The template provides the [state-and-recovery playbook](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery) and regression cases.

### Step 6-2. Own changes and ongoing verification

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Operations owner

Review content freshness and permissions; re-evaluate source, model, skill or connector changes. [Monitor the deployed agent](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/analytics-overview).

Review advisor sessions, failed interactions, tool authentication errors and credit usage in Monitor.

### Step 6-3. Release: ALM

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

Back up the reviewed workspace, pull before editing and pushing, then package with `pac copilot pack`.

### Step 6-4. Release: recovery

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Confirm backup eligibility for the environment type and rehearse restoration to a supported test target.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The recovery rehearsal uses an eligible environment type and a supported restore target.
- [ ] The operator reviews failed sessions, source usage, connection errors and credit consumption after rollout.
